title: Tensor algebra action transported by an additive functor
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A and B commutative R-algebras, and E=A\otimes_R B [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let C be an A-linear preadditive category, K:C\to Mod(B) an additive functor, and Q an object of C. Assume K((r\text{ mapped to }A)\,id_Q)=(r\text{ mapped to }B)\,id_{KQ} for every r\in R. There are an E-module T with carrier in the same universe as KQ and a B-linear isomorphism e:Res_{B\to E}T\cong KQ such that e\circ Res((a\otimes1)\,id_T)=K(a\,id_Q)\circ e for every a\in A. Category and ring universes may differ.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change; Tensor algebra action transported by an additive functor

proof.text: The additive functor gives a ring map on endomorphisms. Compose with A-scalar multiplication; the hypothesis identifies its restriction to R with B-scalars. All these endomorphisms are B-linear and commute with B-scalars. The algebra tensor universal property gives a ring map E to B-linear endomorphisms. Restrict the evaluation module along this map. Its B-action agrees with the original B-action, so identity maps give e. Its A-action is the original ring map, giving the equation. This is implemented in Lean using Algebra.TensorProduct.lift, Module.compHom and an explicit identity-carrier isomorphism.
